questions.q: The word 'science' comes from the Latin word 'Scientia', which means:
questions.explanation: Science is to know about nature.

questions.q: Physics is the branch of science that describes:
options: matter, energy, space, time and their mutual interactions
questions.explanation: This is the book's definition of physics.

questions.q: The two main branches of science are:
questions.explanation: Physical sciences study non-living things; biological sciences study life.

questions.q: Physics is one of the branches of:
questions.explanation: Along with chemistry, geology, astronomy etc.

questions.q: A scientist who specialises in physics is called a:
questions.explanation: Physicists do theoretical and experimental research.

questions.q: The main objective of physics is to:
options: understand the physical world by developing theories based on observations and experiments
questions.explanation: Physicists express natural happenings in mathematical laws.

questions.q: A cell phone locates our position using signals from:
questions.explanation: GPS uses satellites and physics of electromagnetic waves.

questions.q: The sky appears blue because sunlight is:
options: scattered by gas molecules of the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Blue light is scattered the most.

questions.q: Submarines and heavy ships work on the principle of:
questions.explanation: Buoyancy keeps them afloat.

questions.q: Newton's laws fail for objects moving near the speed of light. This was solved by:
questions.explanation: Relativity agrees with Newton at low speeds and is accurate at high speeds.

questions.q: The improvement of Newton's laws by Einstein shows that science is:
questions.explanation: Scientists share knowledge and critique ideas to improve theories.

questions.q: Large lakes keep the climate of nearby land moderate because water has a:
questions.explanation: Water absorbs and releases heat slowly.

quizzes.topic: Branches of Physics and Interdisciplinary Fields

questions.q: The branch of physics that studies light and instruments like spectacles is:
questions.explanation: Optics deals with the nature and properties of light.

questions.q: Studying how air conditioners cool a house belongs to:
questions.explanation: It deals with heat and energy transfer.

questions.q: The branch that deals with neutrons and protons in the nucleus is:
questions.explanation: Structure and behaviour of atomic nuclei.

questions.q: The study of sound is called:
questions.explanation: Production, transmission and reception of sound.

questions.q: The study of the origin, structure and future of the whole universe is:
questions.explanation: Cosmology spans the universe from birth to death.

questions.q: The study of fundamental particles and forces (high energy physics) is:
questions.explanation: Also called high energy physics.

questions.q: Fluid dynamics of blood flow and use of radiation in diagnosis are studied in:
questions.explanation: Physics applied to living systems.

questions.q: The study of the Earth's structure and processes (e.g. earthquakes) using physics is:
questions.explanation: Uses seismic waves and energy transfer.

questions.q: The motion of microscopic particles like electrons is described by:
questions.explanation: Classical mechanics fails at atomic scale.

questions.q: Bodies moving with speeds close to the speed of light are studied in:
questions.explanation: Einstein's relativity.

questions.q: Using computers and numerical analysis to solve complex physics problems is:
questions.explanation: It combines computer science, physics and mathematics.

questions.q: Chemistry uses physics of ______ to understand chemical reactions.
questions.explanation: Physics is the most fundamental science used by others.

questions.q: Which branch of science plays an important role in engineering?
questions.explanation: Engineering applies physical principles.

questions.q: A tentative assumption or explanation made before research that can be tested is a:
questions.explanation: It can be verified or rejected by experiments.

questions.q: A well-supported explanation of some aspect of nature, verified through rigorous testing, is a:
questions.explanation: Theories explain how and why phenomena occur.

questions.q: A statement that summarises an observed regularity in nature and relates variables is a:
questions.explanation: E.g. Newton's laws of motion.

questions.q: Which is an example of a scientific theory?
questions.explanation: Also the theory of general relativity.

questions.q: Which is an example of a scientific law?
questions.explanation: Laws describe a relationship observed in nature.

questions.q: The main difference between laws and theories is:
options: laws describe phenomena, theories explain why they happen
questions.explanation: Laws are narrower; theories focus on how and why.

questions.q: Scientists develop a hypothesis before research mainly because it:
options: helps predict outcomes and define what to test
questions.explanation: It guides the design of experiments.

questions.q: Falsifiability means a theory is scientific only if:
options: it makes claims that could be proven false by evidence
questions.explanation: Scientific ideas must be testable and disprovable.

questions.q: Which statement is NOT falsifiable (not scientific)?
options: Objects fall with acceleration 9.8 m/s² near Earth
Invisible undetectable spirits move the planets
questions.explanation: No experiment could ever test or disprove it.

questions.q: If reliable new evidence contradicts a theory, scientists:
questions.explanation: Science is self-correcting.

questions.q: The best definition of 'theory' in science is:
options: a comprehensive set of ideas explaining a phenomenon in nature
questions.explanation: A theory is supported by a large body of evidence.

questions.q: Science is best described as:
options: systematic study to gain knowledge of how nature works
questions.explanation: Through observation, hypotheses and experiments.

questions.q: Technology is:
options: the application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes (tools, machines, systems)
questions.explanation: It satisfies human needs.

questions.q: Engineering is:
options: the practical use of scientific and mathematical principles to design and build structures, devices and processes
questions.explanation: It solves real-world problems creatively.

questions.q: Studying the laws of motion through experiments is an example of:
questions.explanation: It is pursuit of knowledge.

questions.q: Development of smartphones is an example of:
questions.explanation: Applying physics and materials science to make a device.

questions.q: Designing and building a bridge is mainly:
questions.explanation: Uses materials science and structural mechanics.

questions.q: The relation among science, technology and engineering is that:
options: advances in science lead to new technology, and engineers use science to create technologies that drive further science
questions.explanation: They are distinct but interconnected.

questions.q: Which is an example of technology based on physics?
questions.explanation: It applies electromagnetism and nuclear physics.

questions.q: Asking 'why does the sky look blue?' and testing it belongs to:
questions.explanation: Seeking an explanation of nature.

questions.q: Using knowledge of electromagnetic waves to build a mobile network is:
questions.explanation: Applying scientific knowledge for practical use.

questions.q: In the book's summary, engineering is described as:
options: the process of studying and developing technology
questions.explanation: Technology is tools and methods; engineering develops them.

questions.q: What is the best definition of the term 'theory' as it is used in science?
options: A theory is a guess or hunch about something that has occurred in nature
A theory is a comprehensive set of ideas explaining a phenomenon in nature
A theory is based on verifiable laws and can be proven true
A theory is a hypothesis that uses laws and observation to make an assumption
questions.explanation: A theory is a well-supported, broad explanation of a natural phenomenon.

questions.q: Which statement below correctly identifies the difference between laws and theories?
options: Laws describe phenomena, while theories explain why phenomena exist
Laws are a statement of fact, while theories are a statement of opinion
Laws explain why phenomena exist, while theories explain how
Laws are a prediction of phenomena, while theories are an explanation
questions.explanation: Laws describe what happens; theories explain how and why.

questions.q: Why do scientists develop a hypothesis before conducting research?
options: It gives them direction on how to interpret the results of their research
It helps to predict outcomes and define the parameters of the research
Hypotheses give the researcher an outcome to shape their work around
Hypotheses help a researcher decide which observations to record and which to ignore
questions.explanation: A hypothesis is a testable prediction that frames the investigation.

questions.q: The branch of physics that is most important when studying how glasses help people see:
questions.explanation: Lenses and vision are part of optics.

questions.q: When studying how air conditioners cool your house, the branch is:
questions.explanation: Heat transfer and cooling cycles belong to thermodynamics.

questions.q: The branch of physics that deals with particles such as neutrons and protons:
questions.explanation: Nuclear physics studies the nucleus.

questions.q: Which branch of science plays an important role in engineering?
questions.explanation: Engineering is based on physical principles.

questions.q: Physics is one of the branches of:
questions.explanation: Physics studies non-living matter and energy.
